title: Hearing Polish
summary: Every Polish line can be read aloud; each clip is made once, stored as MP3 and replayed offline.
description:
Every Polish line has a speaker button, and conversations can be read line by line. The voice is a speech model through OpenRouter, because it is the one option that sounds the same on Android and macOS; the platform's own speech engine stands in where there is no key.

A line is paid for once. Raw speech is nearly 3 MB a minute, so clips are encoded to MP3 before they are stored.

requirements.text: A line's audio is generated once and stored, keyed by its exact text, the model and the voice; after that it replays without the network.
Changing the voice never plays a clip made in another voice.
Dialogue lines are read in a female or a male voice according to the speaker; the learner chooses the female voice from 14 and the male voice from 16, each with a preview.
A line has a slow version, stored as a clip of its own.
A clip that came out wrong can be made again, replacing the stored one.
Starting a lesson downloads its lines in the background, in the order they will be heard; this can be switched off per device.
A course's audio can be downloaded in one pass, with progress reported line by line.
Settings shows how many clips are stored and how much space they take per course, and can delete the clips no course uses, or all of them.
Speech is stored as MP3: raw audio from the speech model is encoded before it is stored, at 48 kbit/s for one channel.
A clip that cannot be encoded is stored as it came instead of being lost.
Speech stored as WAV by an earlier version is re-encoded to MP3 in the background at startup, one file at a time, and the database is compacted afterwards.
A re-encoded file gets a new id, and the clip or episode that pointed at the old file points at the new one.
When the same clip is asked for twice at once, it is generated once.
Without an OpenRouter key, the platform's own speech engine is used where the webview has one.

questions: The README still describes every speaker in the ten dialogues being tagged female or male in content files. The built-in collection is gone; is the gender of a dialogue line now always set by the tutor when it makes the line?
